newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists want min wage hike above 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists want min wage hike above 4 pct.

text.p: The French Socialist Party's national council, which met at the weekend, wants a rise of more than four percent in the country's minimum wage, the newspaper Les Echos reported on Monday.
The minimum wage, known as the SMIC, currently stands at 6,406.79 francs per month.
The newspaper Les Echos said the Socialist Party wanted to grant a bigger increase than four percent given after Jacques Chirac was elected conservative president in 1995.
The Communist party, which holds the balance of power in the new Socialist-led government, have been calling for a rise of at least eight percent.
The newspaper suggested that the increase would be between those two figures.
The minimum wage increase is likely to come on July 1 ahead of a planned national conference on wages and jobs to start in September.
France's business community opposes a rise in the minimum wage unless it is accompanied by lower payroll taxes.
